correctness.rationale: Fixing the repaired hub colour decouples all outer edges, so g_h counts the exact maximum agreements in each; the singleton multiplicity forces ordinary hub colour C for k>=2. The universal bound is alpha_C>=k. Explicit parity-dependent sources achieve ordinary distance k+1 and weak distance k+1 from k>=4. Elementary exhaustive pair-type arguments settle weak k=2,3 and K3 is the k=1 boundary. The standalone program enumerated every admissible source and proper target through k=6 and checked witnesses through k=18; its finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Primary works introduce or develop the repair invariants for connected bipartite graphs, odd cycles, complete multipartite graphs, disjoint unions, and general computational recognition, but the inspected claims do not evaluate both villainies on the connected friendship-graph join, nor give the exact per-source formula and the k=4 weak equality threshold. The 2018 thesis could not be fully inspected; this residual risk is recorded explicitly.
residual_risks: Raleigh (2018) thesis full text was blocked by the repository (403); only its abstract was available and no definitive full-text noncoverage conclusion is asserted.
An unindexed theorem under another equivalent repair or hub-gluing terminology could exist; negative searches are not proof of novelty.
General algorithms for arbitrary graphs naturally can recover the result when evaluated, but do not themselves supply this evaluated classification.

value.rationale: Exact closed ordinary and weak values for the entire natural nonmultipartite connected friendship-graph family, plus an O(k) formula for each arbitrary disturbed optimum colouring, clarify when relaxing colour multiplicity does and does not help. The exact weak/ordinary transition at four triangles is structurally motivated by hub-colour freedom and cannot be read off from graph order or bipartite theorems. No broader graph-family theorem is claimed.
